{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I proposed the fish early, since its outline is simple and the forked tail identifies it. The table agreed and Maya's sketch became the plan. My main contribution was the nose joint, which was the last thing keeping the top line from connecting to the start. By eye, about 100 of the 111 standing dominoes were connected when I last checked, and the rest were pale strays. I can't say whether the judge recognized a fish. That depends on the push.

**Execution:** Mixed. I found the nose gap and bridged it from the end of the lead-in instead of redoing the whole top line, which was the right call. But I clipped and knocked over some dominoes near the nose while working there, and a few pale strays ended up around the nose that weren't in the sketch. Leo and Tom spotted them and Tom lifted them. I should have caught these myself. I also said I'd take the upper tail fork, then moved to the nose, and Tom and Leo ended up laying and redoing the fork. I was right to stay on the nose, but I should have said so more clearly. Once the nose was dark, I held off restanding anything there so I wouldn't risk breaking it.

**Collaboration:** I tried to avoid bumping others by asking people to stay clear of the spots I was working on. I gave up the pad to Maya rather than fight over it. I accepted Leo's and Tom's corrections without arguing. Tom, Leo and Maya did most of the body and tail work, and Tom's final walk of the run was important.

**Leadership:** I set the direction early and called out when the nose went dark. I then pushed for hands-off so we wouldn't cause late bumps. I wasn't the only one coordinating, since Maya and Tom did a lot of it too. My own slips near the nose are the part I'd improve."}
